## Maple review 🔴 **Confidence 1/10** · do not merge A member admin's unlink sends the payer's id and always 409s; the billing-write gate and the ingest link lookup both trust stale answers. 1 critical −3 · 4 warnings −4 · tests partial −1 · risk high −1 · 3/3 new units observable Adds billing-org links so sub-orgs are billed through one Autumn customer, across the resolver, routes, ingest lookup and dashboard. Not safe to merge yet: a member's own "Stop billing through" button sends the payer's id and always gets a 409. The three open SchemaErrors in `autumn-tracker` and `turn-runner` are untouched by this diff. - `org_billing_links` and `BillingCustomerResolver` map a member org to the org that pays - `BillingOrgService.link`/`unlink` cancel the member's plans and move its uptime count - Billing routes take a branded `BillingCustomerId`; member writes get a typed 409 - Ingest resolves usage to the billing org with a 2s lookup and last-known fallback ### Before merge - [ ] **Migration** · Check it is safe on production data and with the code still deployed · [`packages/db/drizzle/20261028152213_org_billing_links/migration.sql`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/ab229ea1a96746f8f70a70d9bcea792a35235416/packages/db/drizzle/20261028152213_org_billing_links/migration.sql) - [ ] **Manual** · Grant the `billing_sub_orgs` flag on the paying customer in Autumn before any link is attempted (`docs/billing-orgs.md`) - [ ] **Manual** · The `org_billing_links` migration applies in the prd alchemy deploy; do not run `db:migrate` against prd ### Findings
🔴 Critical · F1 · Member unlink sends the payer's org id, so unlink always answers not_a_member correctness · [`apps/web/src/page/settings/billing/view-account.ts:72`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/ab229ea1a96746f8f70a70d9bcea792a35235416/apps/web/src/page/settings/billing/view-account.ts#L72) For `role: "member"`, `account.billingOrg.orgId` is the paying org (domain `BillingAccount`: "this org itself unless it is a member"), and the handler passes the path segment as `memberOrgId` (`billing.http.ts:554`), which `BillingOrgService.unlink` authorizes on `linkOf(memberOrgId)` (`BillingOrgService.ts:386`). The payer has no link row, so the self-unlink that `update.ts:810` marks `isSelf: account.role === "member"` gets a 409 and a member's admin can never stop billing through the payer. Pass the viewer's own org id instead — add it to `BillingAccount` or read it from the session, not from `billingOrg`. ``` Carry the viewer's own org id (e.g. a `selfOrgId` on `BillingAccount`, or the session org) and send that from `memberSection`; `billedOrgsSection`'s per-member button is already correct. ```
🟠 Warning · F2 · A replayed lookup failure re-arms recent_failures, so ingest never re-reads Postgres correctness · [`apps/ingest/src/autumn.rs:109-111`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/ab229ea1a96746f8f70a70d9bcea792a35235416/apps/ingest/src/autumn.rs#L109-L111) A hit on `recent_failures` (line 82) yields the cached error into the `Err` arm, which inserts it again with a fresh 10s TTL. While an org keeps sending telemetry, every request re-arms the window, `customers` stays empty, and `last_known` is served indefinitely: a link written after one transient Postgres error never reaches ingest, against the 60s bound `docs/billing-orgs.md` states. Insert into `recent_failures` only on a genuinely failed attempt. ``` Move the `recent_failures.insert` into the miss path (`try_get_with_by_ref` failure) instead of the shared `Err` arm, so the 10s window is measured from the failure, not from the last hit. ```
🟠 Warning · F3 · unlink moves the uptime count before the link row is deleted correctness · [`packages/backend/src/services/billing/BillingOrgService.ts:392-396`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/ab229ea1a96746f8f70a70d9bcea792a35235416/packages/backend/src/services/billing/BillingOrgService.ts#L392-L396) `moveUptimeMonitors` meters `-count` off the payer and `+count` onto the member before the delete transaction at 397. If that transaction fails the caller gets a persistence error while the link still stands, so the payer's `uptime_monitors` usage is short the monitors it is still paying for, and the retry reuses the same idempotency key and never corrects it. Delete the row first, then move the count. ``` Delete the link under the advisory lock first and move the count only after the row is gone, keyed by the deleted row's `createdAt`. ```
🟠 Warning · F4 · A failed link read reports a link-cancelled plan as churn correctness · [`apps/api/src/routes/webhooks/autumn.http.ts:84-86`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/ab229ea1a96746f8f70a70d9bcea792a35235416/apps/api/src/routes/webhooks/autumn.http.ts#L84-L86) `readLink` failing with `BillingAccountPersistenceError` is mapped to `Effect.as(false)`, so `billedThroughAnother` is false and both `cancellationsFromBillingUpdated` and `planEventsFromBillingUpdated` run for the member org whose plans `BillingOrgService.link` cancelled at period end. A Postgres blip during a link therefore posts a churn review to Slack and emits plan events for a cancellation that is only billing moving; the 200 answer stops Svix from redelivering. Fail the request (503) on a read error, or treat an unknown link as linked. ``` Drop the catchTag and let `BillingAccountPersistenceError` fail the handler so Svix redelivers, or answer `billedThroughAnother: true` when the read fails. ```
🟠 Warning · F5 · requireOwnBilling gates billing writes on the 60-second link cache correctness · [`packages/backend/src/services/billing/BillingCustomerResolver.ts:91-92`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/ab229ea1a96746f8f70a70d9bcea792a35235416/packages/backend/src/services/billing/BillingCustomerResolver.ts#L91-L92) The resolver ships `readLink` (line 45) for "decisions made right after a link changes, which the cache may not have seen yet", but the write gate reads `billingOrgId`, a value cached for `BILLING_ORG_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` per colo. For up to 60s after a link made in another colo, a now-member org passes `requireOwnBilling` and can attach a plan, open the Stripe portal or edit billing details against its own Autumn customer — a second subscription the billing org never sees. Resolve the write gate through `readLink`. ``` Make `requireOwnBilling` (or the `attach`/`openCustomerPortal`/`updateBillingControls`/billing-details callers) read the link with `readLink` instead of the cached `billingOrgId`, and keep the cache for metering reads. ```

🟠 Warning · F7 · unlink reads the monitor count outside the lock monitor creates hold correctness · [`packages/backend/src/services/billing/BillingOrgService.ts:399-412`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/4d9221910486c52c78ed880c5b6ad15ae27f53fa/packages/backend/src/services/billing/BillingOrgService.ts#L399-L412) `countMonitors` runs before the transaction at 400, so it does not see a create that commits in between: a create inserts its monitor under `pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared(hashtext('org_billing_links'))` (`UptimeMonitorsService.ts:621`) and then meters `+1` to whoever pays at that moment (`UptimeMonitorsService.ts:720` -> `UptimeMonitorAllowance.track`). A monitor created between the read and the delete is charged to the payer but left out of the `count` moved back, so the payer keeps paying for a monitor the member now owns, and the member's own customer is short one. Read the count inside the same transaction, after the exclusive lock and before the delete; `link` at 373 has the same window. ``` Move the count into the transaction: take `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('org_billing_links'))`, then count the member's `UptimeMonitors` with `db.run` (as `countPooledMonitors` does), then delete, and return the count to `trackMonitorMove`. ```

Every transfer bug this function has had (order, count, key) still passes the suite. > [!CAUTION]
> **Member unlink sends the payer's org id, so `unlink` always answers `not_a_member`**
>
> <sub>F1 · Critical · correctness</sub>

For `role: "member"`, `account.billingOrg.orgId` is the paying org (domain `BillingAccount`: "this org itself unless it is a member"), and the handler passes the path segment as `memberOrgId` (`billing.http.ts:554`), which `BillingOrgService.unlink` authorizes on `linkOf(memberOrgId)` (`BillingOrgService.ts:386`). The payer has no link row, so the self-unlink that `update.ts:810` marks `isSelf: account.role === "member"` gets a 409 and a member's admin can never stop billing through the payer. Pass the viewer's own org id instead — add it to `BillingAccount` or read it from the session, not from `billingOrg`.

```
Carry the viewer's own org id (e.g. a `selfOrgId` on `BillingAccount`, or the session org) and send that from `memberSection`; `billedOrgsSection`'s per-member button is already correct.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **A replayed lookup failure re-arms `recent_failures`, so ingest never re-reads Postgres**
>
> <sub>F2 · Warning · correctness</sub>

A hit on `recent_failures` (line 82) yields the cached error into the `Err` arm, which inserts it again with a fresh 10s TTL. While an org keeps sending telemetry, every request re-arms the window, `customers` stays empty, and `last_known` is served indefinitely: a link written after one transient Postgres error never reaches ingest, against the 60s bound `docs/billing-orgs.md` states. Insert into `recent_failures` only on a genuinely failed attempt.

```
Move the `recent_failures.insert` into the miss path (`try_get_with_by_ref` failure) instead of the shared `Err` arm, so the 10s window is measured from the failure, not from the last hit.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **`unlink` moves the uptime count before the link row is deleted**
>
> <sub>F3 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`moveUptimeMonitors` meters `-count` off the payer and `+count` onto the member before the delete transaction at 397. If that transaction fails the caller gets a persistence error while the link still stands, so the payer's `uptime_monitors` usage is short the monitors it is still paying for, and the retry reuses the same idempotency key and never corrects it. Delete the row first, then move the count.

```
Delete the link under the advisory lock first and move the count only after the row is gone, keyed by the deleted row's `createdAt`.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **A failed link read reports a link-cancelled plan as churn**
>
> <sub>F4 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`readLink` failing with `BillingAccountPersistenceError` is mapped to `Effect.as(false)`, so `billedThroughAnother` is false and both `cancellationsFromBillingUpdated` and `planEventsFromBillingUpdated` run for the member org whose plans `BillingOrgService.link` cancelled at period end. A Postgres blip during a link therefore posts a churn review to Slack and emits plan events for a cancellation that is only billing moving; the 200 answer stops Svix from redelivering. Fail the request (503) on a read error, or treat an unknown link as linked.

```
Drop the catchTag and let `BillingAccountPersistenceError` fail the handler so Svix redelivers, or answer `billedThroughAnother: true` when the read fails.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **`requireOwnBilling` gates billing writes on the 60-second link cache**
>
> <sub>F5 · Warning · correctness</sub>

The resolver ships `readLink` (line 45) for "decisions made right after a link changes, which the cache may not have seen yet", but the write gate reads `billingOrgId`, a value cached for `BILLING_ORG_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` per colo. For up to 60s after a link made in another colo, a now-member org passes `requireOwnBilling` and can attach a plan, open the Stripe portal or edit billing details against its own Autumn customer — a second subscription the billing org never sees. Resolve the write gate through `readLink`.

```
Make `requireOwnBilling` (or the `attach`/`openCustomerPortal`/`updateBillingControls`/billing-details callers) read the link with `readLink` instead of the cached `billingOrgId`, and keep the cache for metering reads.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **`unlink` cannot finish the monitor move once the link row is gone**
>
> <sub>F6 · Warning · correctness</sub>

The link row is deleted (lines 393-405) before `moveUptimeMonitors` reads the member's monitor count, so a failed count read leaves the payer's `uptime_monitors` usage still counting monitors it no longer pays for, while the caller gets a 503. Nothing can correct it afterwards: the whole move is keyed off `row.value.createdAt`, and the retry finds no row at line 388 and answers `not_a_member` at line 391. `link` sidesteps exactly this by letting `checkLinkable` return the existing row so a retry finishes the second step.

```
Run `moveUptimeMonitors` before the delete transaction: the `billing_unlink:` key makes a repeated move a no-op, so the same request (or a retry, while the row still exists) finishes the delete instead of stranding the count.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **`unlink` reads the monitor count outside the lock monitor creates hold**
>
> <sub>F7 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`countMonitors` runs before the transaction at 400, so it does not see a create that commits in between: a create inserts its monitor under `pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared(hashtext('org_billing_links'))` (`UptimeMonitorsService.ts:621`) and then meters `+1` to whoever pays at that moment (`UptimeMonitorsService.ts:720` -> `UptimeMonitorAllowance.track`). A monitor created between the read and the delete is charged to the payer but left out of the `count` moved back, so the payer keeps paying for a monitor the member now owns, and the member's own customer is short one. Read the count inside the same transaction, after the exclusive lock and before the delete; `link` at 373 has the same window.

```
Move the count into the transaction: take `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('org_billing_links'))`, then count the member's `UptimeMonitors` with `db.run` (as `countPooledMonitors` does), then delete, and return the count to `trackMonitorMove`.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **`unlink` counts monitors under the link lock, but monitor deletes never take it**
>
> <sub>F10 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`UptimeMonitorsService.delete` takes only `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(orgId))` (`UptimeMonitorsService.ts:895`), never the shared `org_billing_links` lock, so deleting one of the member's monitors can commit between this count and the `-1` that delete tracks to the payer: `unlink` then moves `N` while `N-1` remain, leaving the payer's `uptime_monitors` at `-1` and the member's a monitor too high for good. Take `pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared(hashtext('org_billing_links'))` in the delete transaction too, as `countPooledMonitors` already does for creates; `link`'s count at line 324 has the same gap.

```
Add `select pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared(hashtext('org_billing_links'))` to the `remove` transaction in `UptimeMonitorsService.ts` (next to `lockOrgMonitors`), so the pool cannot change between `unlink`'s count and the delete's `-1`.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **Meter write after the link lock double-counts a monitor a link moved**
>
> <sub>F11 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`create` and `delete` hold the shared `org_billing_links` lock only until commit, and `allowance.track` runs afterwards, re-reading the link uncached (`UptimeMonitorAllowance.track`, line 912 here and line 720 in `create`) to pick the customer. A link or unlink landing in that window has already counted the new or deleted row in `BillingOrgService.countMonitors`, so the move and the `+1`/`-1` land on different customers: the payer ends one short and the member one over for the same monitor.

```
Resolve the paying customer inside the transaction while the shared lock is held, and meter with that `BillingCustomerId` through a `track` variant that takes it, instead of re-reading the link after commit.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **Shutdown flush drops usage whose billing org never resolved**
>
> <sub>F13 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`flush` only sends entries that carry a `customer_id`, so an entry whose `BillingOrgResolver::resolve` fails stays unsealed (autumn.rs:362-364) and the `break` here discards the accumulator: up to one flush interval of already-metered usage is lost, where the removed `flush_all` sent every entry under the org's own id. The case is reachable at a deploy or shutdown while Postgres is down or past `BILLING_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT`, for an org with no `last_known` answer yet; only the `warn!` inside `flush` records it.

```
On the shutdown path, send what resolved and fall back to the org's own id for the entries that did not, or log each dropped `(org_id, feature_id, value)` so the usage can be reconciled.
```
